chunks: Salih ibn 'Uqba from Yunus al-Shaybani who said:

I and Abu Shibl were present with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I asked him about these questions regarding the diyyat (blood money). Then Abu Shibl asked, and he was more intense in his questioning, so I left him until he exhausted (the Imam's answers).

key_terms.أَبُو شِبْلٍ: Abu Shibl (a companion of the Imams)
key_terms.اسْتَنْزَفَ: Exhausted (referring to asking until all knowledge is drawn out)

ai.seo_question: What happened when Salih ibn 'Uqba and Abu Shibl asked Imam al-Sadiq about diyyat?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the scholarly practice of *istifham* (probing inquiry) within the Ahl al-Bayt circles, where Abu Shibl’s persistent questioning highlights the depth of legal nuance in *diyyat* (blood money) jurisprudence. Salih ibn 'Uqba’s role as a patient listener underscores the transmission chain's reliability, while the Imam’s detailed responses establish the foundational principles for compensating the foetus, a key topic in Shia inheritance and tort law.

en.hubeali: Salih Bin Iqba, from Yunus Al Shaybani who said,

‘I and Abu Shibl were present in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about these questions regarding the wergild. The Abu Shibl asked, and he was speaking intensely about it. So I left him until he grasped it’.
